history.summary: An ancient Hindu pilgrimage site at Ram Tirath, about 11 km west of Amritsar on Chogawan Road — TOWN CORRECTED: the CSV town 'Amritsar' is the nearby city; the temple stands at the village of Ram Tirath. Tradition identifies this as the hermitage of Maharishi Valmiki, where Sita took refuge after her exile, where Luv and Kush were born and were taught the Ramayana, and where Valmiki composed the epic. The large sarovar (circumference ~3 km) is said to have been dug by Hanuman, and the Sita baoli step-well is believed to be where Sita bathed; the Punjab District Gazetteer (Amritsar, 1976) notes the site's origin is obscure. The complex, managed by the Valmiki Tirath Development Board, was substantially renovated and reopened in 2016 with a new temple, devotee hall, museum, and an 8-ft gold-plated statue of Valmiki.

name: Ram Tirath Temple
town_description: Ram Tirath is a village on the Chogawan Road about 11 km west of Amritsar, best known for the Valmiki Tirath temple complex. The area is deeply associated with Ramayana lore — Valmiki's hermitage, Sita's refuge, and the birthplace of Luv and Kush — and comes alive during the annual Kartik Purnima fair. The nearest major city is Amritsar, the spiritual centre of Sikhism, whose airport and railway station serve the site.
